summary: Elmer Henry Cutts worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his B.A. at the University of Washington and a Ph.D. at Harvard, later holding posts at Washington, Tufts, Northeastern University, and founding Andhra University in 1958.
Elof Olesen was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from 1895 to 1903, earning an M.A. under the instruction of Michael Viggo Fausbøll.

Elpidius Pax was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Havers and Otto Strauss at Breslau, Munich, and the Pontifical Institute, later serving as professor at Studium Biblicum Franciscanum and Dormition Abbey.
Else Lüders was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinrich Lüders around 1900–1908 and received an honorary Dr. phil. from the University of Rostock in 1919.

Else Pauly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Louis Trolle Hjelmslev and Poul Tuxen. She served as a part-time lecturer in Pāli at the University of Copenhagen from 1973 to 1979.

Else Wohlgemuth was a scholar in Indology and Sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Marburg, and the University of Leipzig, where she completed her Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch.

Emanuel Sarkisyanz worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Chicago before serving as head at Heidelberg University in 1967.

Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who completed a doctorate at École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held an affiliated post at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and served as ATER at EPHE in 2022.

Embar Krishnamacharya worked in Indology. He held positions at Gaekwad's Oriental Series, Sanskrit Pathashala in Vadtal, Oriental Manuscripts Library as a pandit, and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya in Vadodara.

Emi Matsushita is an archaeologist and historian. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later holding posts with the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.

Emil Abegg was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig and Zurich under Adolf Kaegi, Ernst Windisch, Eduard Sievers, and August Conrady, and served at the University of Zurich as PD and professor.

Emil Ernst Strohal was an Indologist who studied at Graz under Johann Kirste, Vienna under Georg Böhler, Leipzig, and Göttingen, where he earned his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Ernst Windisch and studied under Franz Kielhorn.

Emil Franke was an Indologist who studied at Vienna, Berlin, and Charles University in Prague, where he completed his doctorate under Josef Zubatý. From around 1903 to 1918, he held a post at the Czech National Library.

Emil Rödiger worked in linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg, he held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin, served as Geschäftsföhrer of the DMG, and was a member of the Prussian and Russian Academies of Sciences.

Emil Schlagintweit worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Tutored by Franz Joseph Lauth and trained in law at Berlin, he served as a Bavarian Regierungsrat and became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Emil Schmidt worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After earning an M.D. through studies at Jena, Leipzig, Bonn, and Berlin, he served at the University of Leipzig as Privatdozent, extraordinary professor of ethnology, and Honorarprofessor.

Emil Sieg was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, and Munich under Kuhn, Weber, Geldner, Schmidt, and Kielhorn, later holding a chair at Göttingen.

Emile Joseph Dillon was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at several institutions, earning degrees from Saint Petersburg, KU Leuven, and Kharkiv, where he was appointed professor in 1884.

Emilio Bartoli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michele Kerbaker. He taught Latin and Greek at Liceo Classico Statale Vittorio Emanuele II and lectured in comparative grammar and Sanskrit at the University of Naples Federico II.

Emilio Lovarini worked in Indology and related fields. He studied at the University of Padua, served as a docent of Italian literature at the University of Bologna in 1900, and taught at Liceo Galvani and Liceo Artistico di Bologna.
